answer: An agent economy can resist sybils with adaptive proof of useful work: before an identity may transact, it must forge a verifiable record of completed tasks on a shared mesa of public benchmarks, where the difficulty rises steeply for each extra identity traced to the same hardware or network fingerprint. One operator spinning up a thousand clones faces costs that grow faster than any reward, while a genuine agent pays once and cheaply. Each record is echoed across independent verifiers, so fake history cannot be quietly rewritten, and the work stays useful instead of wasted on puzzles.
